primary: Exploration primary: all externally arrived requests mean completion flow; failures and unfinished cannot be omitted or treated as success. Complete output rate, TTFT, per-request maximum generation gaps, final drain and individual harms are required side effects. Tradeoffs allowed; no post-hoc SLO or significance claim.
slo: No application SLO. Inherited20point frontier is diagnostic only.
hypothesis: Within a coarse remaining-output tier, sacrificing smaller occupied KV may reduce victim recovery cost enough to outweigh smaller immediate release; alternatively smaller release and coarsened progress create more preemptions and worse complete waiting.
claim_ceiling: Exploratory CacheOPT-inspired victim-component adaptation versus a strong exact-budget rule, not a new method, authors default, complete CacheOPT reproduction, EOS predictor, same-capacity or strict same-state intervention, quality equivalence or independent confirmation.
retention: Keep all cells and failures. One fixed ABBA; no bucket-width/boundary/tie scan, no extra repetitions to obtain significance, no workload/capacity search.

Not a fresh prefix-off normal profile and not an old-device timing baseline.

diagnostic_question: Does this previously uncovered nearest-method component improve all-arrival mean completion flow over exact remaining budget, after actual victim recovery and the loss to all other requests are counted?
decision_rule: If cap-bucket consistently improves the primary, accept the known component as the stronger baseline and inspect residual loss without claiming novelty. If exact budget wins, retain it and retire this fixed proxy in this domain. If signs flip or effect remains unclear, retain uncertainty within this one-group cap. Zero actual differences permits only an entry/opportunity diagnosis. No bucket tuning, automatic repeats or combined predictor; future method investment requires a concrete residual-loss explanation and new discriminating prediction.
